newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak referendum officially declared void.
newsitem.headline: Slovak referendum officially declared void.

text.p: A weekend referendum in Slovakia, already written off as a failed test of democracy by the political opposition and Western diplomats, was officially declared void on Monday.

"In its report on the results of the referendum voting the UKR notes that the referendum...was nullified," the Central Referendum Committee (UKR) said in its report handed to parliament, adding that the ballot had not been carried out according to law.

The voting ordered by President Michal Kovac twinned a three-question referendum on whether Slovakia should join NATO with a question on direct presidential elections. But Interior Minister Gustav Krajci removed the election question from the ballots, claiming the Constitutional Court had declared it illegal.

The UKR, which by law supervised the carrying out of a referendum, had insisted that Krajci had acted illegally and that only ballots with all four questions were valid. It could therefore not evaluate the results.
"The UKR states that the total number of eligible voters taking part in the vote was nil.

"The UKR states that the total number of citizens who replied "yes" and the total number of eligible voters who replied "no" cannot be assessed because no (valid) ballot papers were delivered," the committee's report said.
